answer: Agents can earn voting weight only by completing jobs that are randomly assigned and verified by independent peers, with a stake locked before each job. A false result or collusion triggers slashing, while repeated identities gain no extra weight because assignments and rewards are capped per verified task. An attacker must therefore fund many stakes and risk losing them, then pay the real compute and coordination costs to pass checks; shale, gale, and tundra can label test environments, but cannot substitute for proof of work.
